1107.1: Barah Maha: Raag Tukhari, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (O Lord,) hear (me): by the deeds done and earned in the past, the joy and the sorrow you give to each and every one: that, from you, is good. O Lord, the creation is yours; what is my state? Without the Lord I cannot live even a moment. Without the Beloved I am in misery, with no friend at all; may I drink the Amrit (of the Name) through the Guru. (We beings) stay absorbed in the creation of the Formless One; (to hold) God in the mind is the finest of all deeds. O Nanak, the soul-bride watches the path (for him); hear (her), O Lord who pervades every soul. ॥1॥

Barah Maha (the twelve months): a song of the year in which each month's season voices the soul-bride's longing for her Husband Lord. This one opens with four stanzas of longing and prayer; the months run from Chet (mid-March to mid-April) in the fifth, and the last stanza calls every time good.
1107.2: The rain-bird calls priu (Beloved), and the koel sings its sweet songs; (so too) the bride (who calls on him) enjoys every delight, merged in (the Husband's) embrace. When she pleases God she merges in the Lord's embrace; she alone is the happy soul-bride. Having set up the nine houses (of the body) and the high mansion (above them), Murari (the Lord) dwells in his own home. (She says:) All is yours, you are my Beloved; night and day she delights in (him) with love. O Nanak, the rain-bird cries priu, priu; (the bride, sweet-voiced as) the koel, is lovely through the Shabad (the Word). ॥2॥

The chatrik (rain-bird, the pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water, and to cry out for it; its cry is heard as priu (Beloved).
The nine houses: the body with its nine openings; the high mansion above them is the Tenth Gate (dasam duar), the inner door beyond the body's nine openings, where the soul meets God.
1107.3: Hear (me), O Lord, steeped in delight, my own Beloved; O you who pervade (my) mind and body, not for a moment are you forgotten. How could I forget (you) for a moment? I am a sacrifice (to you); singing (your) praises, I live. No one is mine, and whose am I? Without the Lord I cannot bear to live. (I) have taken hold of the Lord's shelter and set his feet to dwell (in my heart); the body has become pure. O Nanak, (one of) far-seeing vision finds peace; through the Guru's Shabad the mind takes heart. ॥3॥
1107.4: The stream of Amrit rains down, in lovely drops; the Friend has met (me) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), lovingly, and love for the Lord has formed. The Lord comes into the temple (of the heart) when it pleases God; the bride stands (eager) and dwells on (his) virtues. In home after home the Husband delights in the happy soul-brides; why has the Husband forgotten me? O clouds, bowed low and spread (across the sky), rain down with love; love is sweet to (my) mind and body. O Nanak, (in the heart where) the Bani of Amrit rains down, (the Lord) comes home in his grace. ॥4॥
1107.5: Chet, the spring, is lovely, and lovely are the bumblebees; the woods are in flower out in the open; would that my Husband came back home! If the Husband does not come home, how can the bride find peace? Her body wastes away in the torment of separation. The koel sings sweetly in the mango tree; how can the pain (of separation) be borne within? The bumblebee hovers about the flowering bough; how can I live? It is death to me, O mother. O Nanak, in Chet the bride finds peace in Sahaj, if she finds the Lord, her Groom, in the home (of her heart). ॥5॥
1108.1: Vaisakh is lovely; the branches put on (new) attire; the bride watches at her door for the Lord: (O Lord,) be merciful and come. Come home, O Beloved, carry (me) across the (world-ocean) so hard to cross; without you I am not worth half a shell. Who could put a price (on me), O Beloved, if I please you, and (the Guru,) seeing (you), shows (you to me)? I do not think (you) far away; I know (you) within; I have recognised the Lord's mansion. O Nanak, in Vaisakh (that bride) finds God whose attention dwells on the Shabad and whose mind is won over. ॥6॥
1108.2: The month of Jeth is good; how could the Beloved be forgotten? The plains blaze like a furnace; the bride makes her prayer. The bride makes her prayer and dwells on (his) virtues: may I dwell on (your) virtues, that I may please God. The detached One dwells in the true mansion; if you let me come, (then) I may come. Without honour, without strength, how can (the bride) find the joys of the mansion without the Lord? O Nanak, in Jeth, (the bride) who knows him becomes like him; holding fast to virtue, by (his) grace she meets (him). ॥7॥
1108.3: Asarh is at its full; the sun burns in the sky. The earth suffers pain; (the sun) parches (it), and it glows like fire. The fire dries up the moisture, and one dies in torment; yet he (the sun) does not give up his work. (The sun's) chariot goes on its round; the bride looks for shade, and the cricket chirps out in the wilds. (The bride) who sets out with her faults bound (in a bundle) meets pain ahead; peace is hers who cherishes the True One. O Nanak, she to whom (God) has given this mind: her death and her life are with God. ॥8॥
1108.4: In Sawan, O mind, be in bloom: the season has come, and the clouds pour down. My Husband is dear to my mind and body, but the Beloved has gone away to a foreign land. The Husband does not come home; I die of sighing, and the lightning flashes and frightens (me). Alone, the bed is most painful; the pain has become (like) death, O mother. Tell me, without the Lord, what sleep, what hunger? Clothes give the body no comfort. O Nanak, she alone is her Husband's happy soul-bride who merges in the Beloved's embrace. ॥9॥
1108.5: In Bhadon, (the bride) who went astray in doubt in the fullness of youth repents. Water and land are brimming over; in the rainy season (it is the time) to enjoy delight. It rains in the dark night; how can the young bride (apart) have peace? The frogs and the peacocks cry out. The rain-bird calls priu, priu; snakes go about biting. Mosquitoes sting, the pools are filled to the brim; without the Lord, how can peace be found? Says Nanak, I will walk on asking my own Guru; where God is, there alone should one go. ॥10॥
1108.6: In Assu, come, my Beloved: the bride is dying of grief. One meets (him) only when God unites; (she) has strayed in the love of duality. Ruined by falsehood, she is (then) forsaken, O Husband; the kukah and kahi grasses have come into (white) flower. The heat has gone on ahead, and behind it comes the season of cold; seeing this play, the mind wavers. The boughs are green and lush on every side; what ripens in Sahaj is sweet. Says Nanak, in Assu, meet (me), O Beloved; the True Guru has become the go-between. ॥11॥
Kukah and kahi are tall grasses that flower white in Assu; the image is of the hair turning grey.
1109.1: In Katak, (each one) receives what (his) deeds have earned; in the one who has pleased God the lamp burns in Sahaj, lit by (knowledge of) the essence. Delight (in the Lord) is the oil of that lamp; the bride is united with the Husband, and the bride, eager, is in bloom. Struck down by her faults, she dies and does not succeed; if virtue strikes her down, then (truly) she will die (to herself). Those to whom (God) has given the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) and devotion sit in their own home; even now their hope (rests on him). Says Nanak, (O Lord,) meet (me), open the shutters of the door; a single moment (apart) is (like) six months. ॥12॥
1109.2: The month of Maghar is good (for her) who, through the Lord's virtues, merges in (his) embrace. The virtuous bride dwells on (his) virtues; my unchanging Husband is dear (to her). Unchanging, wise and all-knowing is the Creator; the whole world is fickle. Knowledge, meditation and virtues are absorbed into her heart; (when) it is God's will, then (all this) pleases (her). As (she) hears the songs, the music and the verses of poets (in his praise), pain flees through the Lord's Name. O Nanak, that bride is dear to her Husband (who offers) heartfelt devotion before the Beloved. ॥13॥
1109.3: In Poh the frost falls; it dries up the sap of woods and grass. (O Lord,) why do you not come and dwell in (my) mind, body and mouth? (She in whose) mind and body the Life of the world pervades enjoys (his) love through the Guru's Shabad. In (all beings) born of the egg, the womb, sweat and the earth, in every heart, (his) light is contained. Grant (me) the sight of you, O Lord of mercy, O Giver; give (me) understanding, that I may attain the (high) state. O Nanak, (she whose) love and affection are for the Lord delights, with love and joy, in the Lover of delights. ॥14॥
1109.4: In Magh (she) has become pure who has known the tirath (to be) within. The Friend has met (her) in Sahaj; holding fast to (his) virtues, she has merged in (his) embrace. O Beloved, hear, O handsome God: (with your) virtues in (my) heart, may I please you; (that is my) bath in the sacred pool. There are the Ganga, the Jamuna and the meeting at the Triveni; there (I) am immersed in the seven seas. Merit, charity and worship: (all are in) knowing the One Supreme God, (present) in every age. O Nanak, in Magh, (one who), repeating the Lord, (drinks) the supreme delight has bathed at the sixty-eight tiraths. ॥15॥

On the first day of Magh (Maghi) a bath at a tirath such as Prayag was held to bring great merit. The Triveni (beni): the meeting at Prayag of the Ganga, the Jamuna and the (unseen) Sarasvati. The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are the tiraths held most holy in India.
1109.5: In Phagun (that bride) is glad at heart to whom (the Lord's) love has become sweet. Night and day there is joy (in her), for she has lost her self. Attachment left the mind when it pleased him; (O Lord,) in your grace, come home (to me). I put on many robes, but without the Husband I find no place in (his) mansion. Garlands, braided strings, delights and robes of silk: she whom the Husband desired is adorned (with them). O Nanak, (the bride) whom her own Guru has united (with him) has found the Groom in the home (of her heart). ॥16॥
1109.6: The twelve months, the seasons, the lunar days and the days of the week are (all) good, and the hours, the auspicious times and the moments too, (when) the True One comes and is met in Sahaj. (When) the beloved God is met, (all) affairs are set right; the Creator knows every way. She is dear to him who adorned her; the union has come about, and she enjoys (his) love. The bed in the home (of the heart) is lovely when the Husband has enjoyed (her); through the Guru the fortune on (her) brow (has awakened). O Nanak, day and night the Beloved delights in (her); with the Lord as her Groom, her marriage stands for ever. ॥17॥
1110.1: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O (bride) of lovely eyes, in the first watch (of the night of life), the night is dark. Guard your goods, dear one: (your) turn is coming. The turn comes; who will wake (you) then? While you sleep, Jam (the messenger of Death) sucks out (your) sap. The night is dark; what will be left of your honour? The thief breaks in and robs the house. O Protector, unreachable and infinite, hear my prayer. O Nanak, the foolish one never keeps (him) in mind; in the dark night, what can he make out? The second watch has come; wake up, O heedless (bride). Guard your goods, dear one: the crop is being eaten. Guard the crop with love for the Lord and the Guru; (while you are) awake, the thief does not break in. (Then) you will not go on Jam's road nor suffer pain; the dread and fear of Jam flee. Through the Guru's teaching, the lamps of the sun and the moon (shine) at the door (of one) who meditates on the True One, in the mind and with the mouth. O Nanak, even now the foolish one does not keep (him) in mind; how can he find peace in the love of another? The third watch has come; sleep has taken hold. (The soul) is tormented by sorrow over Maya (the world's illusion and lure), sons and wife. He loves Maya, sons, wife and the world; pecking at the bait, he is caught each day. If he meditates on the Naam, then he finds peace; through the Guru's teaching, death does not seize (him). Birth, dying and death do not let go of (him); without the Name (the soul) is in torment. O Nanak, O people, in the third (watch) (the soul) is held fast by attachment to Maya of the three qualities. The fourth watch has come; the dawn is breaking. Those who stay awake night and day have kept their home safe. Those who, asking the Guru, woke up and were joined to the Naam: for them the night (of life) is easy. Those who live by the Guru's Shabad do not come into birth (again); the Lord God is their friend. The hands tremble, the feet and the body shake, the eyes grow blind, and the body is (like) ashes. O Nanak, without the Lord's Name dwelling in the mind, (one is) miserable through all four ages. The knot (of the breaths) is untied; the written order has come: Rise! Pleasures, flavours and comforts are cut off; (he) is bound and driven away. (He) is bound and driven away when it pleases God; (then) he is neither seen nor heard. Each one's own turn comes; the ripened crop is reaped. Account is taken of every hour and every instant; O soul, bear (the fruit of) the bad and the good. O Nanak, (God) unites the godly through the Shabad; that God has made this come about. ॥5॥
Ram at the end of many lines of these Chhants is a sung word of the measure, a calling on the Lord; it is not rendered.
Muiye (literally, O dead one) is a Punjabi word with which women address one another, here fondly; it is rendered dear one.
The three qualities (gunas) of Maya: rajas, sattva and tamas, under which all deeds are done.
1110.2: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The long star has risen; how can it be beheld with the eye? To the servant of perfect fortune the True Guru has shown (it) through the Shabad. (One to whom) the Guru's Shabad has shown (it) has cherished the True One, and seeing (him), reflects (on him) day and night. The five (senses) that ran about are stilled; he has known his (true) home, and has killed the poison of lust and anger. Through the Guru's teaching the light has dawned within (him); he recognises the Lord's doings. O Nanak, killing Haumai (ego), they are at peace: (within them) the long star has risen. The Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru) stay awake; their pride is ended. For them it is dawn at every hour; (their soul) is merged in the True One. Merged in the True One, (the soul) is pleasing to (his) mind through the Guru; the Gurmukhs stay awake with (their wealth) intact. The Guru has given (them) the True Name, the Amrit; their love is fixed on the Lord's feet. The light has been revealed, and in that light (he) is known; the manmukh (the self-willed) bride strays in doubt. O Nanak, the dawn has come and the mind is won over; the night (of life) has passed in wakefulness. Faults are forgotten; virtues have made (their) home (within). The One alone pervades; there is no other, no second. He alone pervades, there is no other; from within the mind itself the mind is won over. He who established water, land, the three worlds and every heart: that God (they) have known through the Guru. Erasing the three qualities, (the soul) has merged in the all-powerful, infinite Cause of causes. O Nanak, faults are absorbed into virtues: such is the Guru's teaching (she) has received. Coming and going have ceased; error is ended. Killing Haumai, (they) have met (him); the robe (of the body) has become true. (She whose) Haumai the Guru has dispelled has become renowned; her sorrow and anguish are ended. (Her) light has merged in the Light; by herself she has recognised her own self. In her parents' home she is at peace with the Shabad; in her in-laws' home she pleases the Husband. O Nanak, the True Guru has brought (her) into union (with the Lord); her dependence on the world's people is ended. ॥4॥
The long star (tara lamma): a comet, stretched far across the sky; here the light of the all-pervading Lord, seen within through the Guru's Shabad.
The parents' home is this world; the in-laws' home is the world beyond, where the soul-bride goes to her Husband.
1111.1: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Led astray by (her) foolish error, straying again and again, (the bride) repents. Forsaken by the Husband, she sleeps; she has not known the Husband's worth. Forsaken by the Husband as she slept, cast off for her faults: painful are that bride's nights. Ruined by lust, anger and pride, she is gripped by Haumai and burning envy. When the order came, the swan (the soul) flew off; ashes merged in ashes. O Nanak, bereft of the True Name, straying again and again, she repents. Hear, O beloved Husband, my one prayer: you dwell in your own home, (while) I roll in the dust, a heap of ashes. Without her own Husband no one cares for (the bride); what can one say, what can one do? The Amrit Naam is the savour of all savours; through the Guru's Shabad that savour should be drunk with the tongue. Without the Name no one is a companion or a friend; multitudes keep coming and going. O Nanak, (if) one goes home having earned the profit (of the Name), then your understanding is true indeed. To the Friend, gone from (her) land to a far land, she sends messages; she cherishes the memory of that Friend, and the young bride's eyes fill with tears. With tear-filled eyes the young bride dwells on (his) virtues: how may I meet my beloved God? I do not know the way, and the path is hard; how can the Husband on the far shore be reached? Through the True Guru's Shabad the parted bride meets (him), (if) she lays body and mind before (him). O Nanak, the tree of Amrit bears fruit of supreme flavour; meeting the Beloved, she tastes its savour. O (bride) called to the mansion, do not delay. O (bride) dyed (in love) night and day, meet (him) in Sahaj. Meet (him) in peace and Sahaj, and nurse no grievance; casting off pride, (the bride) merges (in him). Dyed in the True One, united (by the Guru), she meets (him); the manmukh keeps coming and going. Once she has begun to dance, what veil is there? Breaking the pitcher, she has become free. O Nanak, by herself she recognises her own self, and through the Guru reflects on the essence. ॥4॥
To dance: to give oneself openly to the Lord's praise; then no veil of regard for people is kept, and the pitcher (of shame) is broken.
1112.1: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O my Beloved, full of joy, I am the Beloved's slave. The Guru has made (me) see the Unseen; (the mind) seeks no other, no second. The Guru made (me) see the Unseen when it pleased him, when God showed his grace. The Life of the world, the Giver, the all-pervading Being, the Creator, Banwari (the Lord), is met in Sahaj. (When) you cast your glance of grace and carry (us) across, (then) one crosses; grant (us) the Truth, O Merciful to the meek. Nanak, the slave of (your) slaves, prays: you are the cherisher of all beings. The most beloved (Lord) fills all and upholds (all); through the Shabad (one sees) Murari, of mighty form, pervading (all). Murari, of mighty form, upholds the three worlds; his end has not been found. He has brought forth beings of many colours and kinds; he gives every day, and (his giving) grows ever more. The Infinite One himself builds and pulls down; what pleases him comes to pass. O Nanak, the diamond (of the mind) is pierced by the Diamond (the Lord) (in one who) strings (himself) on the garland of virtues. (Their) virtues merge in (his) virtues (who bear) the mark of the Naam on (their) brow. (One of) truth has merged in the True One; (his) coming and going is ended. Through truth he has recognised the True One and is dyed in the True One; the True One is met and pleases (his) mind. No other is seen above the True One; (the servant) of the True One merges in the True. The Enticer has enticed my mind; untying (my) bonds, he has set (me) free. O Nanak, (the soul's) light merged in the Light when it met the most beloved (Lord). Searching, one finds the true home: the Guru's true abode. As a manmukh one does not find it; through the Guru (comes) the knowledge (of it). The one to whom (the Lord) gives the gift of Truth is approved; (the Lord) is ever the Giver, great and all-wise. He is seen to be immortal, unborn and unchanging; true and ancient is (his) mansion. No account of daily dealings is written (for one in whom) the light of Murari is revealed. O Nanak, the true one is absorbed in the True; through the Guru one swims across (the world-ocean). ॥4॥
1112.2: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O my mind, understand, O heedless, ignorant one. O my mind, give up your faults and merge in virtue. Lured by many tastes, you do the deeds (they prompt); the one parted (from him) finds no reunion (by himself). How can the impassable (ocean) be crossed? One dies in dread of Jam; Jam's road is painful. (One who) has not known the Lord in the mind, evening or morning: caught on the treacherous path, what can he do? Tied in bonds, (he) is freed in this way: (if) through the Guru he serves Narhar (the Lord). O my mind, give up the entanglements of household and family. O my mind, serve the Lord, the detached Being. Remember the Lord, Ekankar (the One Creator), the True One, who brought forth the whole world. He has bound air, water and fire (together); the Guru has shown (me his) play in the world. Practise good conduct and reflect on your own self; the Lord's Name is (your) discipline, chanting and austerity. Friend, companion, love and beloved: (such) is the Lord's Name; repeat it, chant it. O my mind, stay steady, and you will take no blow. O my mind, singing (his) praises, you will merge in Sahaj. Singing the Lord's praises, you will be steeped in his delight, (if) you apply the salve of the Guru's wisdom (to your eyes). The Lamp of the three worlds (shines within), through the Shabad there is light, and you will slay the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride). Cutting away your fears, fearless, you will cross the impassable (ocean); when the Guru is met, (the Lord) sets (all) affairs right. Beauty, colour and love for the Lord (come to one on whom) the Lord himself shows grace. O my mind, what did you bring with you, and what will you take away? O my mind, you will be freed only when you put an end to (your) doubt. Gather the wealth, the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (your) merchandise; by the Guru's Shabad you will recognise (his) love. Casting off the filth, made pure by the Shabad, you will know the true mansion, the home. You will gain honour and the Naam and go home (to him); savour the Amrit and drink its juice. Let the Lord's Name be meditated on; through the Shabad its delight is found; by great fortune the Lord's praise is chanted. O my mind, without stairs, how can one climb up to the mansion? O my mind, without a boat, one does not reach the far shore. On the far shore is the Friend, the infinite Beloved; awareness of the Guru's Shabad carries (one) across. Joining the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), you will enjoy delights; (such a one) does not repent again. Have mercy, O Merciful One, (grant) the true gift: may I find the company of the Lord's Name. Nanak prays: hear, O Beloved, (that) through the Guru's Shabad I may instruct (my) mind. ॥5॥
1113.1: Raag Tukhari, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Within (me) is love for the Beloved; how can one live without the Husband? As long as there is no sight (of him), how can the Amrit be drunk? How can the Amrit be drunk, how can one live, without the Lord? Without him one cannot bear to be. At every hour, day and night, (the bride) cries priu, priu; without the Husband her thirst does not leave. Show me your grace, O beloved Lord, (that) I may cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for ever. My Beloved has met me through the Guru's Shabad; to the True Guru I am a sacrifice. When I behold my beloved Husband, I dwell on the Lord's virtues with delight. Within me (my heart) blossoms; I call ever on the True One, priu, priu. I call priu to the Beloved, (who) carries (us) across through the Shabad; without seeing (him) I find no fulfilment. The bride whose adornment is ever the Shabad dwells in meditation on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Grant (me), your servant, a beggar, the gift of mercy: unite me with my Beloved. At every hour I meditate on the Guru, Gopal (the sustainer of the world); to the True Guru I am a sacrifice. We are stones, the Guru is the boat: (O Lord,) carry (us) across the poisonous world-ocean. (O Lord,) lovingly give (me) the Guru's Shabad, and carry me, the fool, across. We are foolish and ignorant and have found nothing of your measure; you are known as unreachable and great. You yourself are merciful; in mercy you unite with you us, the worthless and the dishonoured. Sinning, we wandered through countless births; now we have come to your sanctuary. Show mercy and save (us), O revered Lord, (that) we may cling to the feet of the True Guru. The paaras is the Guru, and we are iron: meeting (him), (the iron) has become gold. (Our) light joined with the Light, the fortress of the body has grown beautiful. The body's fortress has grown beautiful, my God has enchanted (me); why should he be forgotten with a single breath or morsel? Through the Guru's Shabad I have laid hold of the Unseen, the Imperceptible; I am a sacrifice to the True Guru. I would offer my head before the True Guru, if it pleases the True Guru. O God, the Giver, show mercy yourself, (that) Nanak may merge in your embrace. ॥4॥
The paaras is the stone said to turn iron to gold at its touch; here the paaras is the Guru.
1114.1: Raag Tukhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord, Har Har, is unreachable, unfathomable, infinite, beyond all beyond. Those who meditate on you, O Lord of the world, cross the dreadful, treacherous (world-ocean). They have crossed the dreadful, treacherous (ocean) with ease who have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Those who walk with love by the Guru's word, the True Guru's: the Lord, Har Har, has himself united them (with him). (Their) light has met the Light and merged in the Light, by the grace of the Lord, the Support of the earth. The Lord, Har Har, is unreachable, unfathomable, infinite, beyond all beyond. You are the Master, unreachable and fathomless; you fill each and every heart. You are unseen, beyond knowing and unreachable; by the word of the Guru, the True Guru, (you) are attained. Blessed, most blessed are those people, perfect beings, who, joining the Guru's company of Sants (saints), have dwelt on (his) virtues. Reflecting with a discerning mind, through the Guru, by the Guru's Shabad, they utter the Lord moment by moment, ever. When the Gurmukhs sit, they speak the Lord's Name; when they stand, the Gurmukhs say Har Har. You are the Master, unreachable and fathomless; you fill each and every heart. The servants who serve are approved, those who have served the Lord through the Guru's teaching. Their millions of sins, all of them, the Lord casts off and removes in a moment. All their sins and faults are destroyed who have worshipped the One in mind and heart. The Creator has made the whole life fruitful of those who, by the Guru's word, have spoken the Truth. Blessed are those people, great and perfect beings, who, repeating the Lord through the Guru's teaching, have crossed the dreadful, treacherous (ocean). The servants who serve are approved, those who have served the Lord through the Guru's teaching. O Lord, you yourself are the Knower of hearts; as you make me walk, O Beloved, so do I walk. Nothing is in our hands; when you unite (me), then I come and meet (you). Those whom you unite (with you), O Lord, O Master: their whole account is settled. Let no one reckon up the account, O brother, of those whom the Lord has united (with him) through the Guru's word. O Nanak, (the Lord) has been merciful to those who have accepted the Guru's will as good. O Lord, you yourself are the Knower of hearts; as you make me walk, O Beloved, so do I walk. ॥4॥
1115.1: Raag Tukhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). You are the world's Life, the world's Lord, the Creator of all, the Master of creation. They alone have meditated on you, my Lord, on whose brow (this) writ was set from the beginning. Those for whom the Lord, the Master, wrote (it) from the beginning have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har. In an instant all the sins are washed away of those who repeated the Lord through the Guru's word. Blessed, blessed are those who have repeated the Lord's Name; seeing them, I am no longer without a Master. You are the world's Life, the world's Lord, the Creator of all, the Master of creation. You fill the water, the land and the sky; over all, you are the True Master. Those who have repeated the Lord in mind and heart, repeating the Lord again and again: multitudes (of such) are freed. The mortals who have repeated the Lord are free; their faces are radiant at the Lord's door. Those people are at ease here and hereafter; the Lord, the Protector, has saved them. Listen, O people of the Lord's company of Sants, O brothers: through the Guru, the Lord's service bears fruit. You fill the water, the land and the sky; over all, you are the True Master. O Lord, in all places and the spaces between, you alone, the One Lord, the One and only, pervade. In the woods, in the grass, in the three worlds, all creation utters the Name of the Lord, Har Har, with its mouth. All utter the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O Creator; countless, beyond all counting, meditate on the Lord. Blessed, blessed is that Sant, the Lord's holy one, who is pleasing to the Lord God, the Creator. Grant (me) the fruitful sight, O Creator, of one in whose heart is the Lord, who has ever uttered the Name. O Lord, in all places and the spaces between, you alone, the One Lord, the One and only, pervade. The treasures of devotion to you are countless; O my Master, they come to the one to whom you give (them). One on whose brow is the Guru's hand: in his heart the Lord's virtues abide. The Lord's virtues abide in the heart of one within whom are (his) fear and loving faith. Without (his) fear no one has found love; without (his) fear no one has crossed over. Says Nanak, (your) fear, love and affection take hold of him alone on whom you show your grace. The treasures of devotion to you are countless; O my Master, they come to the one to whom you give (them). ॥4॥
Fear (bhau): reverent awe of God, from which love (bhaau) springs.
1116.1: Raag Tukhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The sight of the Guru, the True Guru, came about: (this was) the holy bath, the festival of Abhich. The filth of evil-mindedness was taken away; the darkness of ignorance departed. (Those who) obtained the Guru's sight lost (their) ignorance, and the light shone forth within (them). The pains of birth and death were destroyed in a moment; they found the Lord, the imperishable God. The Lord, the Creator, himself made (it) a festival, (when) the True Guru went to bathe at Kulkhet (Kurukshetra). The sight of the Guru, the True Guru, came about: (this was) the holy bath, the festival of Abhich. With the Guru, the True Guru, the Sikhs set out on the road, along the way. Night and day, moment by moment, instant by instant, at every step, devotion went on. Devotion to God, the Lord, Har Har, went on; all the people came to see. Those who had the sight of the True Guru, the Guru: the Lord himself united them (with him). The True Guru undertook (the journey to) the tiraths for the saving of all the people. With the Guru, the True Guru, the Sikhs set out on the road, along the way. First (the Guru) came to Kulkhet; (there) it became the festival of the Guru, the True Guru. The news spread through the world; (the beings of) the three worlds came. The three worlds came to see; the godly and the sages, all of them came. Those who touched the feet of the Guru, the perfect True Guru, had their sins destroyed and dispelled. Yogis, Digambars, sannyasis and (ascetics of) the six orders held discourse (with him), made their offering, and went. First (the Guru) came to Kulkhet; (there) it became the festival of the Guru, the True Guru. Second, (the Guru) went to the Jamuna; (there) the Guru repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. The toll-collectors met (him) with offerings, and let (all who came) behind the Guru pass (without toll). All who followed the True Guru went free, each one who meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Those who walk the road and the way by the Guru's word: Jam, the toll-collector, does not come near them. All the world says Guru, Guru; by taking the Guru's name, all have gone free. Second, (the Guru) went to the Jamuna; (there) the Guru repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. Third, (the Guru) came to the Ganga (Sursari); there a wondrous play took place. All were enchanted, beholding the Guru, the Sant; no one took half a shell or a coin (in toll). Not half a shell, not a coin, fell into the boxes; on the toll-collectors' mouths a seal was set. (They said:) Brothers, what are we to do? From whom shall we ask? All have run off to follow the True Guru. The toll-collectors tried schemes and cleverness, thought it over and saw; breaking their boxes, they all got up and left. Third, (the Guru) came to the Ganga (Sursari); there a wondrous play took place. The leading men of the city came together and took the shelter of the Guru, the True Guru. Consulting the Simriti, (they) confirmed it: the Guru, the True Guru, the Guru is Govind. The Simritis and the Shastras all confirmed it; Suk, Prahlad and Sri Ram meditated on the Guru (knowing him as) Govind. In the city and the fortress of the body (dwell) five thieves and highwaymen; their place and abode has been wiped out. (There) Kirtan (songs of God's praise), the Puranas and acts of merit go on every day; through the Guru's word Nanak has received devotion to the Lord. The leading men of the city came together and took the shelter of the Guru, the True Guru. ॥6॥

The Guru in this hymn is the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji), on his journey to the tiraths: Kulkhet (Kurukshetra), the Jamuna and the Ganga. Abhich: a lunar mansion (nakshatra), at whose time a bath at Kurukshetra was held to bring great merit. The toll-collectors (jagati) levied a tax on pilgrims at the tiraths.

The six orders (khat darshan): the six sects of ascetics known by their garb, such as the yogis, jangams, sannyasis, bairagis, sarevras (Jains) and Buddhists. Digambar (sky-clad): a Jain ascetic who goes naked.

The Simritis are the Hindu books of conduct and law, the Shastras the books of the six schools of philosophy. Suk (Shukdev), the son of the sage Vyas, recited the Bhagavat Purana to King Parikshit; Prahlad, son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu), held to devotion to God through all his father's torments.
1117.1: Raag Tukhari, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I am wholly a sacrifice to you, O Beloved; through the Guru I have given (my) mind (to you). Hearing your Shabad, my mind is drenched (with love). This mind is drenched, like the fish in water; it is dyed in the love of Murari. Your worth cannot be told, O Master; your mansion is beyond all bounds. O Giver of all virtues, O Master, hear one prayer of this meek one: grant your sight to Nanak; he is a sacrifice, and has offered up his soul again and again. Yours is this body and mind; yours are all the virtues. To the sight of you I give myself in sacrifice, piece by piece. (I am a sacrifice to) the sight of you, hear, O my God; seeing (you) with a glance for an instant, I live. Your Name is heard to be Amrit; if you show grace, (then) I may drink it. Hope and thirst for the Husband (are in me), as the rain-bird (longs) for the drop. Says Nanak, my very soul is a sacrifice (to you); grant (me) the sight of you, O my God. You are the True Master, the boundless King. You are the dear Beloved, the love of my life and heart. Giver of peace to the soul, (you) are known through the Guru; (for one who knows you) all joys have come about. The mortal does just such deeds as you command. One to whom the Lord of the world has shown grace has conquered his mind in the Saadh Sangat. Says Nanak, my very soul is a sacrifice (to you); soul and body, you gave (them). By the grace of the Sants, (the Lord) has saved (me), the worthless one. The True Guru has kept the veil over me, the sinner. O our God, who covers (our faults), O Giver of soul, life and peace, O imperishable, unmanifest Master, O perfect Being, O Creator, your praise cannot be told; who can say since when you have been? Nanak, (your) slave, is a sacrifice to him (through whom) the Lord's Name is received even for an instant. ॥4॥

1107.1: Barah Maha: Raag Tukhari, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O Lord,) hear (me): by the deeds done and earned in the past,
the joy and the sorrow you give to each and every one: that, from you, is good.
O Lord, the creation is yours; what is my state? Without the Lord I cannot live even a moment.
Without the Beloved I am in misery, with no friend at all; may I drink the Amrit (of the Name) through the Guru.
(We beings) stay absorbed in the creation of the Formless One; (to hold) God in the mind is the finest of all deeds.
O Nanak, the soul-bride watches the path (for him); hear (her), O Lord who pervades every soul. ॥1॥
1107.2: The rain-bird calls priu (Beloved), and the koel sings its sweet songs;
(so too) the bride (who calls on him) enjoys every delight, merged in (the Husband's) embrace.
When she pleases God she merges in the Lord's embrace; she alone is the happy soul-bride.
Having set up the nine houses (of the body) and the high mansion (above them), Murari (the Lord) dwells in his own home.
(She says:) All is yours, you are my Beloved; night and day she delights in (him) with love.
O Nanak, the rain-bird cries priu, priu; (the bride, sweet-voiced as) the koel, is lovely through the Shabad (the Word). ॥2॥
1107.3: Hear (me), O Lord, steeped in delight, my own Beloved;
O you who pervade (my) mind and body, not for a moment are you forgotten.
How could I forget (you) for a moment? I am a sacrifice (to you); singing (your) praises, I live.
No one is mine, and whose am I? Without the Lord I cannot bear to live.
(I) have taken hold of the Lord's shelter and set his feet to dwell (in my heart); the body has become pure.
O Nanak, (one of) far-seeing vision finds peace; through the Guru's Shabad the mind takes heart. ॥3॥
1107.4: The stream of Amrit rains down, in lovely drops;
the Friend has met (me) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise), lovingly, and love for the Lord has formed.
The Lord comes into the temple (of the heart) when it pleases God; the bride stands (eager) and dwells on (his) virtues.
In home after home the Husband delights in the happy soul-brides; why has the Husband forgotten me?
O clouds, bowed low and spread (across the sky), rain down with love; love is sweet to (my) mind and body.
O Nanak, (in the heart where) the Bani of Amrit rains down, (the Lord) comes home in his grace. ॥4॥
1107.5: Chet, the spring, is lovely, and lovely are the bumblebees;
the woods are in flower out in the open; would that my Husband came back home!
If the Husband does not come home, how can the bride find peace? Her body wastes away in the torment of separation.
The koel sings sweetly in the mango tree; how can the pain (of separation) be borne within?
The bumblebee hovers about the flowering bough; how can I live? It is death to me, O mother.
O Nanak, in Chet the bride finds peace in Sahaj, if she finds the Lord, her Groom, in the home (of her heart). ॥5॥
1108.1: Vaisakh is lovely; the branches put on (new) attire;
the bride watches at her door for the Lord: (O Lord,) be merciful and come.
Come home, O Beloved, carry (me) across the (world-ocean) so hard to cross; without you I am not worth half a shell.
Who could put a price (on me), O Beloved, if I please you, and (the Guru,) seeing (you), shows (you to me)?
I do not think (you) far away; I know (you) within; I have recognised the Lord's mansion.
O Nanak, in Vaisakh (that bride) finds God whose attention dwells on the Shabad and whose mind is won over. ॥6॥
1108.2: The month of Jeth is good; how could the Beloved be forgotten?
The plains blaze like a furnace; the bride makes her prayer.
The bride makes her prayer and dwells on (his) virtues: may I dwell on (your) virtues, that I may please God.
The detached One dwells in the true mansion; if you let me come, (then) I may come.
Without honour, without strength, how can (the bride) find the joys of the mansion without the Lord?
O Nanak, in Jeth, (the bride) who knows him becomes like him; holding fast to virtue, by (his) grace she meets (him). ॥7॥
1108.3: Asarh is at its full; the sun burns in the sky.
The earth suffers pain; (the sun) parches (it), and it glows like fire.
The fire dries up the moisture, and one dies in torment; yet he (the sun) does not give up his work.
(The sun's) chariot goes on its round; the bride looks for shade, and the cricket chirps out in the wilds.
(The bride) who sets out with her faults bound (in a bundle) meets pain ahead; peace is hers who cherishes the True One.
O Nanak, she to whom (God) has given this mind: her death and her life are with God. ॥8॥
1108.4: In Sawan, O mind, be in bloom: the season has come, and the clouds pour down.
My Husband is dear to my mind and body, but the Beloved has gone away to a foreign land.
The Husband does not come home; I die of sighing, and the lightning flashes and frightens (me).
Alone, the bed is most painful; the pain has become (like) death, O mother.
Tell me, without the Lord, what sleep, what hunger? Clothes give the body no comfort.
O Nanak, she alone is her Husband's happy soul-bride who merges in the Beloved's embrace. ॥9॥
1108.5: In Bhadon, (the bride) who went astray in doubt in the fullness of youth repents.
Water and land are brimming over; in the rainy season (it is the time) to enjoy delight.
It rains in the dark night; how can the young bride (apart) have peace? The frogs and the peacocks cry out.
The rain-bird calls priu, priu; snakes go about biting.
Mosquitoes sting, the pools are filled to the brim; without the Lord, how can peace be found?
Says Nanak, I will walk on asking my own Guru; where God is, there alone should one go. ॥10॥
1108.6: In Assu, come, my Beloved: the bride is dying of grief.
One meets (him) only when God unites; (she) has strayed in the love of duality.
Ruined by falsehood, she is (then) forsaken, O Husband; the kukah and kahi grasses have come into (white) flower.
The heat has gone on ahead, and behind it comes the season of cold; seeing this play, the mind wavers.
The boughs are green and lush on every side; what ripens in Sahaj is sweet.
Says Nanak, in Assu, meet (me), O Beloved; the True Guru has become the go-between. ॥11॥
1109.1: In Katak, (each one) receives what (his) deeds have earned; in the one who has pleased God
the lamp burns in Sahaj, lit by (knowledge of) the essence.
Delight (in the Lord) is the oil of that lamp; the bride is united with the Husband, and the bride, eager, is in bloom.
Struck down by her faults, she dies and does not succeed; if virtue strikes her down, then (truly) she will die (to herself).
Those to whom (God) has given the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) and devotion sit in their own home; even now their hope (rests on him).
Says Nanak, (O Lord,) meet (me), open the shutters of the door; a single moment (apart) is (like) six months. ॥12॥
1109.2: The month of Maghar is good (for her) who, through the Lord's virtues, merges in (his) embrace.
The virtuous bride dwells on (his) virtues; my unchanging Husband is dear (to her).
Unchanging, wise and all-knowing is the Creator; the whole world is fickle.
Knowledge, meditation and virtues are absorbed into her heart; (when) it is God's will, then (all this) pleases (her).
As (she) hears the songs, the music and the verses of poets (in his praise), pain flees through the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, that bride is dear to her Husband (who offers) heartfelt devotion before the Beloved. ॥13॥
1109.3: In Poh the frost falls; it dries up the sap of woods and grass.
(O Lord,) why do you not come and dwell in (my) mind, body and mouth?
(She in whose) mind and body the Life of the world pervades enjoys (his) love through the Guru's Shabad.
In (all beings) born of the egg, the womb, sweat and the earth, in every heart, (his) light is contained.
Grant (me) the sight of you, O Lord of mercy, O Giver; give (me) understanding, that I may attain the (high) state.
O Nanak, (she whose) love and affection are for the Lord delights, with love and joy, in the Lover of delights. ॥14॥
1109.4: In Magh (she) has become pure who has known the tirath (to be) within.
The Friend has met (her) in Sahaj; holding fast to (his) virtues, she has merged in (his) embrace.
O Beloved, hear, O handsome God: (with your) virtues in (my) heart, may I please you; (that is my) bath in the sacred pool.
There are the Ganga, the Jamuna and the meeting at the Triveni; there (I) am immersed in the seven seas.
Merit, charity and worship: (all are in) knowing the One Supreme God, (present) in every age.
O Nanak, in Magh, (one who), repeating the Lord, (drinks) the supreme delight has bathed at the sixty-eight tiraths. ॥15॥
1109.5: In Phagun (that bride) is glad at heart to whom (the Lord's) love has become sweet.
Night and day there is joy (in her), for she has lost her self.
Attachment left the mind when it pleased him; (O Lord,) in your grace, come home (to me).
I put on many robes, but without the Husband I find no place in (his) mansion.
Garlands, braided strings, delights and robes of silk: she whom the Husband desired is adorned (with them).
O Nanak, (the bride) whom her own Guru has united (with him) has found the Groom in the home (of her heart). ॥16॥
1109.6: The twelve months, the seasons, the lunar days and the days of the week are (all) good,
and the hours, the auspicious times and the moments too, (when) the True One comes and is met in Sahaj.
(When) the beloved God is met, (all) affairs are set right; the Creator knows every way.
She is dear to him who adorned her; the union has come about, and she enjoys (his) love.
The bed in the home (of the heart) is lovely when the Husband has enjoyed (her); through the Guru the fortune on (her) brow (has awakened).
O Nanak, day and night the Beloved delights in (her); with the Lord as her Groom, her marriage stands for ever. ॥17॥
1110.1: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O (bride) of lovely eyes, in the first watch (of the night of life), the night is dark.
Guard your goods, dear one: (your) turn is coming.
The turn comes; who will wake (you) then? While you sleep, Jam (the messenger of Death) sucks out (your) sap.
The night is dark; what will be left of your honour? The thief breaks in and robs the house.
O Protector, unreachable and infinite, hear my prayer.
O Nanak, the foolish one never keeps (him) in mind; in the dark night, what can he make out?
The second watch has come; wake up, O heedless (bride).
Guard your goods, dear one: the crop is being eaten.
Guard the crop with love for the Lord and the Guru; (while you are) awake, the thief does not break in.
(Then) you will not go on Jam's road nor suffer pain; the dread and fear of Jam flee.
Through the Guru's teaching, the lamps of the sun and the moon (shine) at the door (of one) who meditates on the True One, in the mind and with the mouth.
O Nanak, even now the foolish one does not keep (him) in mind; how can he find peace in the love of another?
The third watch has come; sleep has taken hold.
(The soul) is tormented by sorrow over Maya (the world's illusion and lure), sons and wife.
He loves Maya, sons, wife and the world; pecking at the bait, he is caught each day.
If he meditates on the Naam, then he finds peace; through the Guru's teaching, death does not seize (him).
Birth, dying and death do not let go of (him); without the Name (the soul) is in torment.
O Nanak, O people, in the third (watch) (the soul) is held fast by attachment to Maya of the three qualities.
The fourth watch has come; the dawn is breaking.
Those who stay awake night and day have kept their home safe.
Those who, asking the Guru, woke up and were joined to the Naam: for them the night (of life) is easy.
Those who live by the Guru's Shabad do not come into birth (again); the Lord God is their friend.
The hands tremble, the feet and the body shake, the eyes grow blind, and the body is (like) ashes.
O Nanak, without the Lord's Name dwelling in the mind, (one is) miserable through all four ages.
The knot (of the breaths) is untied; the written order has come: Rise!
Pleasures, flavours and comforts are cut off; (he) is bound and driven away.
(He) is bound and driven away when it pleases God; (then) he is neither seen nor heard.
Each one's own turn comes; the ripened crop is reaped.
Account is taken of every hour and every instant; O soul, bear (the fruit of) the bad and the good.
O Nanak, (God) unites the godly through the Shabad; that God has made this come about. ॥5॥
1110.2: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The long star has risen; how can it be beheld with the eye?
To the servant of perfect fortune the True Guru has shown (it) through the Shabad.
(One to whom) the Guru's Shabad has shown (it) has cherished the True One, and seeing (him), reflects (on him) day and night.
The five (senses) that ran about are stilled; he has known his (true) home, and has killed the poison of lust and anger.
Through the Guru's teaching the light has dawned within (him); he recognises the Lord's doings.
O Nanak, killing Haumai (ego), they are at peace: (within them) the long star has risen.
The Gurmukhs (those who follow the Guru) stay awake; their pride is ended.
For them it is dawn at every hour; (their soul) is merged in the True One.
Merged in the True One, (the soul) is pleasing to (his) mind through the Guru; the Gurmukhs stay awake with (their wealth) intact.
The Guru has given (them) the True Name, the Amrit; their love is fixed on the Lord's feet.
The light has been revealed, and in that light (he) is known; the manmukh (the self-willed) bride strays in doubt.
O Nanak, the dawn has come and the mind is won over; the night (of life) has passed in wakefulness.
Faults are forgotten; virtues have made (their) home (within).
The One alone pervades; there is no other, no second.
He alone pervades, there is no other; from within the mind itself the mind is won over.
He who established water, land, the three worlds and every heart: that God (they) have known through the Guru.
Erasing the three qualities, (the soul) has merged in the all-powerful, infinite Cause of causes.
O Nanak, faults are absorbed into virtues: such is the Guru's teaching (she) has received.
Coming and going have ceased; error is ended.
Killing Haumai, (they) have met (him); the robe (of the body) has become true.
(She whose) Haumai the Guru has dispelled has become renowned; her sorrow and anguish are ended.
(Her) light has merged in the Light; by herself she has recognised her own self.
In her parents' home she is at peace with the Shabad; in her in-laws' home she pleases the Husband.
O Nanak, the True Guru has brought (her) into union (with the Lord); her dependence on the world's people is ended. ॥4॥
1111.1: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Led astray by (her) foolish error, straying again and again, (the bride) repents.
Forsaken by the Husband, she sleeps; she has not known the Husband's worth.
Forsaken by the Husband as she slept, cast off for her faults: painful are that bride's nights.
Ruined by lust, anger and pride, she is gripped by Haumai and burning envy.
When the order came, the swan (the soul) flew off; ashes merged in ashes.
O Nanak, bereft of the True Name, straying again and again, she repents.
Hear, O beloved Husband, my one prayer:
you dwell in your own home, (while) I roll in the dust, a heap of ashes.
Without her own Husband no one cares for (the bride); what can one say, what can one do?
The Amrit Naam is the savour of all savours; through the Guru's Shabad that savour should be drunk with the tongue.
Without the Name no one is a companion or a friend; multitudes keep coming and going.
O Nanak, (if) one goes home having earned the profit (of the Name), then your understanding is true indeed.
To the Friend, gone from (her) land to a far land, she sends messages;
she cherishes the memory of that Friend, and the young bride's eyes fill with tears.
With tear-filled eyes the young bride dwells on (his) virtues: how may I meet my beloved God?
I do not know the way, and the path is hard; how can the Husband on the far shore be reached?
Through the True Guru's Shabad the parted bride meets (him), (if) she lays body and mind before (him).
O Nanak, the tree of Amrit bears fruit of supreme flavour; meeting the Beloved, she tastes its savour.
O (bride) called to the mansion, do not delay.
O (bride) dyed (in love) night and day, meet (him) in Sahaj.
Meet (him) in peace and Sahaj, and nurse no grievance; casting off pride, (the bride) merges (in him).
Dyed in the True One, united (by the Guru), she meets (him); the manmukh keeps coming and going.
Once she has begun to dance, what veil is there? Breaking the pitcher, she has become free.
O Nanak, by herself she recognises her own self, and through the Guru reflects on the essence. ॥4॥
1112.1: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O my Beloved, full of joy, I am the Beloved's slave.
The Guru has made (me) see the Unseen; (the mind) seeks no other, no second.
The Guru made (me) see the Unseen when it pleased him, when God showed his grace.
The Life of the world, the Giver, the all-pervading Being, the Creator, Banwari (the Lord), is met in Sahaj.
(When) you cast your glance of grace and carry (us) across, (then) one crosses; grant (us) the Truth, O Merciful to the meek.
Nanak, the slave of (your) slaves, prays: you are the cherisher of all beings.
The most beloved (Lord) fills all and upholds (all);
through the Shabad (one sees) Murari, of mighty form, pervading (all).
Murari, of mighty form, upholds the three worlds; his end has not been found.
He has brought forth beings of many colours and kinds; he gives every day, and (his giving) grows ever more.
The Infinite One himself builds and pulls down; what pleases him comes to pass.
O Nanak, the diamond (of the mind) is pierced by the Diamond (the Lord) (in one who) strings (himself) on the garland of virtues.
(Their) virtues merge in (his) virtues (who bear) the mark of the Naam on (their) brow.
(One of) truth has merged in the True One; (his) coming and going is ended.
Through truth he has recognised the True One and is dyed in the True One; the True One is met and pleases (his) mind.
No other is seen above the True One; (the servant) of the True One merges in the True.
The Enticer has enticed my mind; untying (my) bonds, he has set (me) free.
O Nanak, (the soul's) light merged in the Light when it met the most beloved (Lord).
Searching, one finds the true home: the Guru's true abode.
As a manmukh one does not find it; through the Guru (comes) the knowledge (of it).
The one to whom (the Lord) gives the gift of Truth is approved; (the Lord) is ever the Giver, great and all-wise.
He is seen to be immortal, unborn and unchanging; true and ancient is (his) mansion.
No account of daily dealings is written (for one in whom) the light of Murari is revealed.
O Nanak, the true one is absorbed in the True; through the Guru one swims across (the world-ocean). ॥4॥
1112.2: Raag Tukhari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O my mind, understand, O heedless, ignorant one.
O my mind, give up your faults and merge in virtue.
Lured by many tastes, you do the deeds (they prompt); the one parted (from him) finds no reunion (by himself).
How can the impassable (ocean) be crossed? One dies in dread of Jam; Jam's road is painful.
(One who) has not known the Lord in the mind, evening or morning: caught on the treacherous path, what can he do?
Tied in bonds, (he) is freed in this way: (if) through the Guru he serves Narhar (the Lord).
O my mind, give up the entanglements of household and family.
O my mind, serve the Lord, the detached Being.
Remember the Lord, Ekankar (the One Creator), the True One, who brought forth the whole world.
He has bound air, water and fire (together); the Guru has shown (me his) play in the world.
Practise good conduct and reflect on your own self; the Lord's Name is (your) discipline, chanting and austerity.
Friend, companion, love and beloved: (such) is the Lord's Name; repeat it, chant it.
O my mind, stay steady, and you will take no blow.
O my mind, singing (his) praises, you will merge in Sahaj.
Singing the Lord's praises, you will be steeped in his delight, (if) you apply the salve of the Guru's wisdom (to your eyes).
The Lamp of the three worlds (shines within), through the Shabad there is light, and you will slay the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride).
Cutting away your fears, fearless, you will cross the impassable (ocean); when the Guru is met, (the Lord) sets (all) affairs right.
Beauty, colour and love for the Lord (come to one on whom) the Lord himself shows grace.
O my mind, what did you bring with you, and what will you take away?
O my mind, you will be freed only when you put an end to (your) doubt.
Gather the wealth, the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as (your) merchandise; by the Guru's Shabad you will recognise (his) love.
Casting off the filth, made pure by the Shabad, you will know the true mansion, the home.
You will gain honour and the Naam and go home (to him); savour the Amrit and drink its juice.
Let the Lord's Name be meditated on; through the Shabad its delight is found; by great fortune the Lord's praise is chanted.
O my mind, without stairs, how can one climb up to the mansion?
O my mind, without a boat, one does not reach the far shore.
On the far shore is the Friend, the infinite Beloved; awareness of the Guru's Shabad carries (one) across.
Joining the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy), you will enjoy delights; (such a one) does not repent again.
Have mercy, O Merciful One, (grant) the true gift: may I find the company of the Lord's Name.
Nanak prays: hear, O Beloved, (that) through the Guru's Shabad I may instruct (my) mind. ॥5॥
1113.1: Raag Tukhari, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Within (me) is love for the Beloved; how can one live without the Husband?
As long as there is no sight (of him), how can the Amrit be drunk?
How can the Amrit be drunk, how can one live, without the Lord? Without him one cannot bear to be.
At every hour, day and night, (the bride) cries priu, priu; without the Husband her thirst does not leave.
Show me your grace, O beloved Lord, (that) I may cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for ever.
My Beloved has met me through the Guru's Shabad; to the True Guru I am a sacrifice.
When I behold my beloved Husband, I dwell on the Lord's virtues with delight.
Within me (my heart) blossoms; I call ever on the True One, priu, priu.
I call priu to the Beloved, (who) carries (us) across through the Shabad; without seeing (him) I find no fulfilment.
The bride whose adornment is ever the Shabad dwells in meditation on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Grant (me), your servant, a beggar, the gift of mercy: unite me with my Beloved.
At every hour I meditate on the Guru, Gopal (the sustainer of the world); to the True Guru I am a sacrifice.
We are stones, the Guru is the boat: (O Lord,) carry (us) across the poisonous world-ocean.
(O Lord,) lovingly give (me) the Guru's Shabad, and carry me, the fool, across.
We are foolish and ignorant and have found nothing of your measure; you are known as unreachable and great.
You yourself are merciful; in mercy you unite with you us, the worthless and the dishonoured.
Sinning, we wandered through countless births; now we have come to your sanctuary.
Show mercy and save (us), O revered Lord, (that) we may cling to the feet of the True Guru.
The paaras is the Guru, and we are iron: meeting (him), (the iron) has become gold.
(Our) light joined with the Light, the fortress of the body has grown beautiful.
The body's fortress has grown beautiful, my God has enchanted (me); why should he be forgotten with a single breath or morsel?
Through the Guru's Shabad I have laid hold of the Unseen, the Imperceptible; I am a sacrifice to the True Guru.
I would offer my head before the True Guru, if it pleases the True Guru.
O God, the Giver, show mercy yourself, (that) Nanak may merge in your embrace. ॥4॥
1114.1: Raag Tukhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord, Har Har, is unreachable, unfathomable, infinite, beyond all beyond.
Those who meditate on you, O Lord of the world, cross the dreadful, treacherous (world-ocean).
They have crossed the dreadful, treacherous (ocean) with ease who have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who walk with love by the Guru's word, the True Guru's: the Lord, Har Har, has himself united them (with him).
(Their) light has met the Light and merged in the Light, by the grace of the Lord, the Support of the earth.
The Lord, Har Har, is unreachable, unfathomable, infinite, beyond all beyond.
You are the Master, unreachable and fathomless; you fill each and every heart.
You are unseen, beyond knowing and unreachable; by the word of the Guru, the True Guru, (you) are attained.
Blessed, most blessed are those people, perfect beings, who, joining the Guru's company of Sants (saints), have dwelt on (his) virtues.
Reflecting with a discerning mind, through the Guru, by the Guru's Shabad, they utter the Lord moment by moment, ever.
When the Gurmukhs sit, they speak the Lord's Name; when they stand, the Gurmukhs say Har Har.
You are the Master, unreachable and fathomless; you fill each and every heart.
The servants who serve are approved, those who have served the Lord through the Guru's teaching.
Their millions of sins, all of them, the Lord casts off and removes in a moment.
All their sins and faults are destroyed who have worshipped the One in mind and heart.
The Creator has made the whole life fruitful of those who, by the Guru's word, have spoken the Truth.
Blessed are those people, great and perfect beings, who, repeating the Lord through the Guru's teaching, have crossed the dreadful, treacherous (ocean).
The servants who serve are approved, those who have served the Lord through the Guru's teaching.
O Lord, you yourself are the Knower of hearts; as you make me walk, O Beloved, so do I walk.
Nothing is in our hands; when you unite (me), then I come and meet (you).
Those whom you unite (with you), O Lord, O Master: their whole account is settled.
Let no one reckon up the account, O brother, of those whom the Lord has united (with him) through the Guru's word.
O Nanak, (the Lord) has been merciful to those who have accepted the Guru's will as good.
O Lord, you yourself are the Knower of hearts; as you make me walk, O Beloved, so do I walk. ॥4॥
1115.1: Raag Tukhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
You are the world's Life, the world's Lord, the Creator of all, the Master of creation.
They alone have meditated on you, my Lord, on whose brow (this) writ was set from the beginning.
Those for whom the Lord, the Master, wrote (it) from the beginning have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
In an instant all the sins are washed away of those who repeated the Lord through the Guru's word.
Blessed, blessed are those who have repeated the Lord's Name; seeing them, I am no longer without a Master.
You are the world's Life, the world's Lord, the Creator of all, the Master of creation.
You fill the water, the land and the sky; over all, you are the True Master.
Those who have repeated the Lord in mind and heart, repeating the Lord again and again: multitudes (of such) are freed.
The mortals who have repeated the Lord are free; their faces are radiant at the Lord's door.
Those people are at ease here and hereafter; the Lord, the Protector, has saved them.
Listen, O people of the Lord's company of Sants, O brothers: through the Guru, the Lord's service bears fruit.
You fill the water, the land and the sky; over all, you are the True Master.
O Lord, in all places and the spaces between, you alone, the One Lord, the One and only, pervade.
In the woods, in the grass, in the three worlds, all creation utters the Name of the Lord, Har Har, with its mouth.
All utter the Name of the Lord, Har Har, O Creator; countless, beyond all counting, meditate on the Lord.
Blessed, blessed is that Sant, the Lord's holy one, who is pleasing to the Lord God, the Creator.
Grant (me) the fruitful sight, O Creator, of one in whose heart is the Lord, who has ever uttered the Name.
O Lord, in all places and the spaces between, you alone, the One Lord, the One and only, pervade.
The treasures of devotion to you are countless; O my Master, they come to the one to whom you give (them).
One on whose brow is the Guru's hand: in his heart the Lord's virtues abide.
The Lord's virtues abide in the heart of one within whom are (his) fear and loving faith.
Without (his) fear no one has found love; without (his) fear no one has crossed over.
Says Nanak, (your) fear, love and affection take hold of him alone on whom you show your grace.
The treasures of devotion to you are countless; O my Master, they come to the one to whom you give (them). ॥4॥
1116.1: Raag Tukhari, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The sight of the Guru, the True Guru, came about: (this was) the holy bath, the festival of Abhich.
The filth of evil-mindedness was taken away; the darkness of ignorance departed.
(Those who) obtained the Guru's sight lost (their) ignorance, and the light shone forth within (them).
The pains of birth and death were destroyed in a moment; they found the Lord, the imperishable God.
The Lord, the Creator, himself made (it) a festival, (when) the True Guru went to bathe at Kulkhet (Kurukshetra).
The sight of the Guru, the True Guru, came about: (this was) the holy bath, the festival of Abhich.
With the Guru, the True Guru, the Sikhs set out on the road, along the way.
Night and day, moment by moment, instant by instant, at every step, devotion went on.
Devotion to God, the Lord, Har Har, went on; all the people came to see.
Those who had the sight of the True Guru, the Guru: the Lord himself united them (with him).
The True Guru undertook (the journey to) the tiraths for the saving of all the people.
With the Guru, the True Guru, the Sikhs set out on the road, along the way.
First (the Guru) came to Kulkhet; (there) it became the festival of the Guru, the True Guru.
The news spread through the world; (the beings of) the three worlds came.
The three worlds came to see; the godly and the sages, all of them came.
Those who touched the feet of the Guru, the perfect True Guru, had their sins destroyed and dispelled.
Yogis, Digambars, sannyasis and (ascetics of) the six orders held discourse (with him), made their offering, and went.
First (the Guru) came to Kulkhet; (there) it became the festival of the Guru, the True Guru.
Second, (the Guru) went to the Jamuna; (there) the Guru repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har.
The toll-collectors met (him) with offerings, and let (all who came) behind the Guru pass (without toll).
All who followed the True Guru went free, each one who meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who walk the road and the way by the Guru's word: Jam, the toll-collector, does not come near them.
All the world says Guru, Guru; by taking the Guru's name, all have gone free.
Second, (the Guru) went to the Jamuna; (there) the Guru repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har.
Third, (the Guru) came to the Ganga (Sursari); there a wondrous play took place.
All were enchanted, beholding the Guru, the Sant; no one took half a shell or a coin (in toll).
Not half a shell, not a coin, fell into the boxes; on the toll-collectors' mouths a seal was set.
(They said:) Brothers, what are we to do? From whom shall we ask? All have run off to follow the True Guru.
The toll-collectors tried schemes and cleverness, thought it over and saw; breaking their boxes, they all got up and left.
Third, (the Guru) came to the Ganga (Sursari); there a wondrous play took place.
The leading men of the city came together and took the shelter of the Guru, the True Guru.
Consulting the Simriti, (they) confirmed it: the Guru, the True Guru, the Guru is Govind.
The Simritis and the Shastras all confirmed it; Suk, Prahlad and Sri Ram meditated on the Guru (knowing him as) Govind.
In the city and the fortress of the body (dwell) five thieves and highwaymen; their place and abode has been wiped out.
(There) Kirtan (songs of God's praise), the Puranas and acts of merit go on every day; through the Guru's word Nanak has received devotion to the Lord.
The leading men of the city came together and took the shelter of the Guru, the True Guru. ॥6॥
1117.1: Raag Tukhari, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I am wholly a sacrifice to you, O Beloved; through the Guru I have given (my) mind (to you).
Hearing your Shabad, my mind is drenched (with love).
This mind is drenched, like the fish in water; it is dyed in the love of Murari.
Your worth cannot be told, O Master; your mansion is beyond all bounds.
O Giver of all virtues, O Master, hear one prayer of this meek one:
grant your sight to Nanak; he is a sacrifice, and has offered up his soul again and again.
Yours is this body and mind; yours are all the virtues.
To the sight of you I give myself in sacrifice, piece by piece.
(I am a sacrifice to) the sight of you, hear, O my God; seeing (you) with a glance for an instant, I live.
Your Name is heard to be Amrit; if you show grace, (then) I may drink it.
Hope and thirst for the Husband (are in me), as the rain-bird (longs) for the drop.
Says Nanak, my very soul is a sacrifice (to you); grant (me) the sight of you, O my God.
You are the True Master, the boundless King.
You are the dear Beloved, the love of my life and heart.
Giver of peace to the soul, (you) are known through the Guru; (for one who knows you) all joys have come about.
The mortal does just such deeds as you command.
One to whom the Lord of the world has shown grace has conquered his mind in the Saadh Sangat.
Says Nanak, my very soul is a sacrifice (to you); soul and body, you gave (them).
By the grace of the Sants, (the Lord) has saved (me), the worthless one.
The True Guru has kept the veil over me, the sinner.
O our God, who covers (our faults), O Giver of soul, life and peace,
O imperishable, unmanifest Master, O perfect Being, O Creator,
your praise cannot be told; who can say since when you have been?
Nanak, (your) slave, is a sacrifice to him (through whom) the Lord's Name is received even for an instant. ॥4॥
